groups.kindClassHelp: A home class such as 7A. Every student in it follows the class's lessons.

requirements.title: Curriculum
requirements.subtitle: How many lessons each class needs per subject and week
requirements.summary: {lessons} lessons in the busiest week · {hours} of teaching per year
requirements.hoursCaveat: Hours count the academic year's calendar weeks and deduct holidays and staff days: a whole break week disappears, a single staff day takes a fifth of its week. It is an estimate at requirement level — a requirement says how many lessons a week, never on which weekdays, so nothing can know whether the staff day fell on one of this subject's lesson days. Right averaged over a term, wrong for any single week.
requirements.hoursCaveatNoBreaks: No holidays or staff days have been entered for this academic year, so the hours count every calendar week and read roughly 8–10 weeks high. Enter the year's breaks under Breaks and they will be deducted here.
requirements.tableCaption: Curriculum by group and subject. The last column is the group's teaching hours per academic year, counted over the year's calendar weeks with holidays and staff days deducted — an estimate, because a requirement does not say on which weekdays the subject is taught.
requirements.empty: No curriculum yet. The AI engine needs this to build a schedule.
requirements.noYear: Create and activate an academic year first.
requirements.loadFailed: No figures are shown, because they would read zero for the wrong reason. Switch the year above to try again.
requirements.loadFailedHint: No figures are shown, because they would read zero for the wrong reason. Switch the year above to try again.
requirements.coTeacherHint: Both teachers are scheduled together; published lessons get a LEAD + ASSISTANT pair.

constraints.title: Availability
constraints.subtitle: When teachers, rooms or classes are unavailable
constraints.empty: No constraints. The AI engine will treat every resource as always available.
constraints.preferencesHint: State what should preferably happen, as opposed to the absolute rules above. The engine tries to honour these but will break a wish rather than make the week unschedulable.
constraints.preferenceWeightHint: How much the engine may give up elsewhere to honour the wish. The scale is the one the optimization profile uses: 5 weighs the same as the other preferences, above 10 the wish starts overriding goals such as spreading subjects across the week.
constraints.gradeHint: The rule applies to every class and teaching group with students in the range.
constraints.locksHint: A lock is absolute: the subject's lessons may only be in the rooms you choose. If it cannot be honoured the timetable is refused, naming the rule that is impossible — unlike the wishes below, which the solver weighs against everything else.
constraints.locksEmpty: No locks. Every room is allowed for every subject.
constraints.ruleGradesHint: The rule applies to a group whose years all fit inside the span. A group spanning 6-7 is therefore not reached by a rule for 7-9.

frameTimes.title: Frame times
frameTimes.subtitle: The hours each stage may be timetabled within
frameTimes.empty: No frame times. The whole school day is open to every year.
frameTimes.hint: A frame time says when a stage MAY have lessons. Everything outside it is closed — the engine places nothing there, the timetable warns if you drag something into it, and the gap search stops offering the time.
frameTimes.overlapHint: Frame times reaching the same group all apply at once, so the narrowest window wins. Writing “08:00–15:00 every day” and “08:00–13:00 Friday” makes Friday 08:00–13:00 with nothing to remove.
frameTimes.effectiveHint: Computed from the rows above, one stage per row.
frameTimes.duplicate: A frame time already exists for those years on that day.

lunchServings.title: Lunch sittings
lunchServings.subtitle: When each stage eats, and in what order
lunchServings.seatsHint: Left blank, the dining hall's own seat count from the lunch card applies.
lunchServings.empty: No sittings. The whole lunch window is open to every year at once.
lunchServings.hint: You write when a stage eats. The solver decides which class goes when inside the window, and splits a stage bigger than the hall into several waves.
lunchServings.overlapHint: Sittings reaching the same group add up — a year 6-7 group may eat at both the 4-6 and the 7-9 sitting. A row for one weekday replaces the every-day row that day rather than widening it.
lunchServings.noLunch: Lunch is not defined — sittings mean nothing until it is.
lunchServings.flowSubtitle: Who eats when, day by day — the list the kitchen can print
lunchServings.flowEmpty: No sittings yet. Generate a timetable and the solver fills them in.
lunchServings.windowsHint: Computed from the rows above, with the rule the solver uses.

breaks.title: Holidays and staff days
breaks.intro: The days the academic year has but the timetable does not. They are deducted from the curriculum's hours, and saving one removes any published lessons inside it from the calendar.
breaks.namePlaceholder: Autumn half term, Staff day, Work experience year 9…
breaks.datesHint: Both days are included. A single staff day has the same date in both fields.
breaks.gradeHint: The break applies to every class with students in the span. Teaching groups without a year of their own are not affected — their lessons stay and remain visible in the calendar.
breaks.deletesWarning: Saving removes published lessons inside the period from the calendar. Lessons that have already happened, been cancelled, or had attendance recorded are left alone. Shortening or deleting the break does not bring back lessons that were already removed.
breaks.removedLessons: {name} saved. {count, plural, =1 {1 published lesson was removed from the calendar.} other {# published lessons were removed from the calendar.}}
breaks.removedNone: {name} saved. No published lessons needed removing.
breaks.deleteBody: The break leaves the list and the curriculum's hours count that week as taught again. The lessons removed when the break was entered do not come back.
breaks.empty: No holidays entered for this academic year. The curriculum's hours then count every calendar week as taught, which runs roughly 8–10 weeks high across a Swedish academic year.
breaks.noYear: Create and activate an academic year first.
breaks.loadFailed: The list of holidays could not be fetched.
breaks.loadFailedHint: No list is shown, because an empty one would mean the school has no holidays at all. Switch the year above to try again.
breaks.tableCaption: The academic year's holidays and staff days, earliest first. Each row is a period the school is not teaching, and the curriculum's hours deduct it.

generate.title: Generate schedule
generate.subtitle: The AI engine builds an optimal weekly timetable from your curriculum and constraints
generate.running: Optimizing… this can take up to a minute
generate.statusTIMEOUT: The solver ran out of time
generate.infeasibleHint: The constraints are too tight. Review the conflicts below, relax availability or reduce lessons per week, then try again.
generate.timeoutHint: The solver did not find a schedule within its time budget. This does not mean your requirements are impossible — try running it again, or ask your administrator to raise the solver time limit. Relaxing tight availability windows also makes a schedule easier to find.
generate.profileHint: Tune what the solver optimizes for. Higher = more important. Saved on this device and sent with every run.
generate.historyHint: Previous optimization runs for this academic year.
generate.rulesHint: The rules apply to the whole school and are set under Availability.
generate.ruleMaxPerDay: Max lessons per day per class

timetable.title: Master timetable
timetable.subtitle: The recurring weekly template produced by the AI engine
timetable.publishBody: Turns the weekly template into dated lessons for the whole year. Lessons already in the calendar are left untouched — to replace them, delete them first.
timetable.empty: No master timetable yet. Generate a schedule first.
timetable.editBody: Move the lesson or change its room and teacher. The change is checked against the rest of the timetable.
timetable.propagateHint: Future published lessons without recorded attendance are moved along automatically.
timetable.editSaved: Lesson updated — {count} calendar lessons moved along
timetable.addBody: Manually place a lesson on the master timetable. It is checked against the rest of the timetable before saving.
timetable.deleted: Lesson removed — {count} future calendar lessons cleaned up
timetable.lockHint: Locked lessons survive regeneration — the optimizer plans around them.
timetable.dragHint: Drag lessons to move, drag the bottom edge to resize, click an empty slot to add, shift-click to multi-select.
timetable.versionsBody: Save named snapshots of the timetable and roll back at any time. A safety snapshot is taken automatically before every restore.
timetable.versionsEmpty: No snapshots yet. Save one before making big changes.
timetable.suggestTitle: That slot is taken — here are the nearest free ones
timetable.suggestBody: These placements are conflict-free for this lesson's class, teacher and room.
timetable.suggestNone: No conflict-free slot found this week. Try changing the room or teacher.
timetable.diffIdentical: The current timetable is identical to this snapshot.
timetable.keyboardHint: Tip: focus a lesson and use arrow keys to move it; Enter opens the editor.
timetable.remoteEditingWarning: {name} is editing this lesson right now — your save may overwrite theirs.
timetable.slotFinderHint: Searches the week for times when the selected class(es) are free — matched with the class's subject teacher first, or a free fallback teacher of the subject.
timetable.slotFinderNone: No open slot with a free subject teacher found. Try fewer classes or a shorter lesson.
timetable.recurrenceHint: Odd and even follow the calendar week number — what you tell the students. Two subjects can share a slot when one runs odd weeks and the other even.
timetable.periodHint: Leave empty for the whole academic year. Fill in for a subject read for part of it, such as half a term.
timetable.editRemoved: {count, plural, =1 {1 calendar lesson was removed — publish again to restore any the window still covers.} other {# calendar lessons were removed — publish again to restore any the window still covers.}}
timetable.sharedMoveTitle: This lesson belongs to several classes
timetable.sharedMoveBody: Moving it moves it for {classes}. Pupils in those classes get the new time in their timetables.

csvImport.importingIntoYear: The rows will be imported into {year}.

csvImport.updatesNotDeletes: The import adds new rows and updates the ones already there. Rows you removed from the file are NOT removed from the curriculum, and a column the file does not have is left alone. But an EMPTY cell in a column the file does have clears that field — that is how you remove a teacher or a period. To remove a whole entry, click it in the table.

lunch.title: Lunch and dining hall
lunch.hint: The solver keeps a lunch break free for every class and staggers the sittings so the dining hall is never over-filled.
lunch.seatsHint: Left empty, the solver assumes everyone can eat at once.
lunch.maxPerDayHint: Applies per class and teaching group.
lunch.notDefined: Lunch has not been defined yet
lunch.publishWarning: No lunch break is reserved. You can still publish, but students may be given lessons in the middle of lunch.

gaps.title: Gaps and idle time
gaps.intro: Three questions asked of the base schedule: when are these free at the same time, where are the idle gaps, and who is free right then. All of it is computed in the browser from the schedule you already have — nothing is saved.
gaps.emptyHint: Generate or lay a schedule first, and there will be gaps to search.
gaps.freeHint: Pick the classes, teachers and rooms that must be free at the same time. The answer is the whole window, not every fifteen minutes — so you can see how much room you actually have to move into.
gaps.freeNobody: Pick at least one class, teacher or room — otherwise the question is about nobody.
gaps.freeNone: No shared free time of at least {minutes} for {who}. Try a shorter length or fewer of them.
gaps.freeCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 free window} other {# free windows}} for {who}
gaps.idleHint: An idle gap is a hole between the first and the last lesson of a day — time somebody spends waiting at school. It is counted per pupil, so a gap can be half a class while the other half is in a lesson. Time before the first and after the last lesson does not count; they are not here for it. Heaviest week first.
gaps.idleLunchWindow: {minutes} min of lunch is credited once a day, to the first gap in the window that can hold it.
gaps.idleLunchOff: No lunch break is configured, so no gap is credited for a meal.
gaps.idleNone: No idle gaps of at least {minutes} anywhere in the schedule.
gaps.idleCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 class or teacher has idle gaps} other {# classes and teachers have idle gaps}}
gaps.idleSummary: Up to {total} idle in a single week, longest gap {worst}
gaps.idleStudents: {free} of {total, plural, =1 {1 pupil free} other {# pupils free}}
gaps.lengthLegend: Gaps are labelled by the waiting time left once lunch is subtracted — the same time the totals are counted in: under 40 minutes is short, 40–79 medium, 80 minutes and up long. A 1 h 40 min gap with 30 min of lunch therefore counts as 70 minutes: medium.
gaps.whoHint: Give a day and a time — the question you ask when you need a substitute on Wednesday at ten. Every class, teacher and room is tested on its own.
gaps.whoInvalid: The end time must be after the start time.
gaps.whoCount: {groups, plural, =1 {1 class} other {# classes}}, {teachers, plural, =1 {1 teacher} other {# teachers}} and {rooms, plural, =1 {1 room} other {# rooms}} are free {day} {start}–{end}

rasts.title: Breaks
rasts.subtitle: When each stage is not taught
rasts.hint: A break is minutes of the day a stage is free. The solver places no lessons across them, and they appear in the pupil's, guardian's and teacher's schedule. Several breaks a day is normal — every matching row applies.
rasts.name: Name
rasts.empty: No breaks have been entered. Without them the solver places lessons back to back.
rasts.weekHint: The rows above read as a week. A day-specific break replaces only the every-day break whose time it overlaps — the others still stand that day.
rasts.deleteBody: {name} will be removed. The solver may then place lessons in that time on its next run.
